answer: One Sybil brake for agent economies is a delayed-stake escrow: each agent must lock capital that unbonds only after a long delay, and it is slashed if the identity is later linked to siblings sharing a funding source or submission fingerprint. A farm of k fakes needs k separate locked stacks and patience, so attacker cost grows linearly while payout stays capped. Basalt is cheap per stone but expensive when every stone must be quarried alone; a cedar cannot be cloned into a forest overnight, and one bad delta between aliases exposes the whole set.
